name: the map starts with {0: 1}
hook: This function counts subarrays that sum to k. Delete the {0: 1} it starts with and it still runs. It just counts wrong.
hook_slide: Delete `{0: 1}` and it still runs. *It just counts wrong.*
hook_sub: Counting the subarrays that sum to k, in one pass.
caption: How many contiguous subarrays sum to exactly k? You don't know the endpoints in advance, so the obvious answer tries every start and every end: {brute_reads} additions for {n} numbers.

The turn: a subarray's sum is one running total minus an earlier one. So at each position, ask a hash map whether an earlier running total equaled running - k. One question per number: {map_reads} steps, same answer.

The map starts with {0: 1}, the empty prefix before index 0. Without it, a subarray that starts at index 0 has no earlier total to match. On {small} with k = {small_k} the answer is {small_with}. Without the seed you get {small_without}. No error, just a wrong count.
And unlike a sliding window, it works with negative numbers: it never shrinks anything.
Have you ever shipped an off-by-one that never crashed? 👇
cta: Next in the module: 2D prefix sums.

p: You don't know the range's endpoints in advance. You're searching for them.
A subarray's sum is one running total minus an earlier one.
So at each position: has an earlier running total equaled `running - k`?
A hash map remembers every running total so far. Each position asks it a single O(1) question.
It is the empty prefix, before index 0. Without it, a subarray that starts at index 0 has no earlier total to match.

rows.lab: Subarrays that sum to {k}, both ways

p: A sliding window needs a guarantee, typically all non-negative values, for its shrink step to be right.
This never shrinks anything. It asks a hash map a question at every position, so negative numbers are fine.
The cost: O(n) space instead of O(1).
